title: FigDown publication manifest (profile 1)
description: The SHAPE contract for the non-core publication manifest of spec/figdown-manifest.md — a sidecar `X.manifest.json` beside a published `X.fd` ⇔ `X.svg` pair, carrying identity, hashes, provenance, review state and dependencies, and nothing else (decisions/registry.md; ruled whole 2026-08-22 as `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`). `accessibility.role` (`MANIFEST-ACCESSIBILITY-ROLE`) landed the same day, closing a gap `ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE` opened that morning against a block that had already shipped closed. It states what tools/manifest-check.js (gate:manifest) validates every manifest against. Like spec/figdown-model.schema.json it states SHAPE only: it cannot check that a restated field agrees with the artifact it restates (assertion B), that a review or accessibility state is bound to the CURRENT source hash rather than a stale one (assertion C's STALE/UNBOUND distinction), or that a well-formed `x-` key is reported rather than silently accepted (assertion E's second half) — those are the verifier's job, run alongside this schema, never instead of it.
$comment: CLOSED, exactly as the language and the model schema are (figdown-manifest.md §3 rule 1; spec/figdown-model.schema.json's own $comment): `additionalProperties: false` at every object level, so an unknown key is an error, never ignored. The ONE extension door is `x-`-prefixed keys, and the extension policy is RULED (`LANGUAGE-EXTENSION-POLICY`/`MANIFEST-EXTENSION-NAMESPACE`, 2026-08-23; figdown-manifest.md §3 rule 2 and §3.1). WHAT THE PATTERN NOW MEANS: the RULED SPELLING is `x-<owner>-<key>`, where `<owner>` is a token the owner controls and can be traced to (a DNS label they hold, a GitHub org, a registered project name) — `x-acme-review-queue`, not `x-queue` — so the pattern `^x-[^-]+(-[^-]+)+$` enforces exactly that and nothing more: at least two non-empty hyphen-separated segments after `x-`, which is the minimum an owner-prefixed key can have. An UNOWNED `x-` key (`x-status`) matches neither `properties` nor this pattern and FAILS, which is the collision `MANIFEST-EXTENSION-NAMESPACE` rule (a) exists to prevent: two publishers, one spelling, two meanings, both files valid. THERE IS NO REGISTRY, no allocation and no application — the namespace is delegated to the owner rather than administered by this project, so nothing here enumerates owners and nothing ever will. A key matching the pattern validates against `{}` (anything): the ruling constrains the SPELLING and the CONSUMER's duties (never infer, always reportable, never revise — figdown-manifest.md §3.1(b)), and deliberately imposes no shape on the value, because the value is the owner's. PROMOTION IS NEVER BY RENAME (`MANIFEST-EXTENSION-NAMESPACE` rule (d), RFC 6648 Appendix B): an `x-` key never becomes a profile key by keeping or changing its spelling, so no future edit of this file will move a name out of `patternProperties` into `properties`. ENUM POLICY: `provenance[].relation`, `review.state`, `accessibility.state`, `accessibility.role` and `dependencies[].kind` are enumerated because a new member of any of them is a semantic event that changes what a consumer may conclude (figdown-manifest.md §4.5, §4.6, §4.7; `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`, `MANIFEST-REVIEW-STATE`, `MANIFEST-ACCESSIBILITY-ROLE`; decisions/registry.md, `ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE`/`ACCESSIBLE-DESCRIPTION-SOURCES`) — the same policy spec/figdown-model.schema.json states for the model's own enums. `renderer.name` is a free string with no enum, because its membership lives in the world of renderer implementations, not in this profile. NO `elements` KEY EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS SCHEMA: per-element provenance was RULED, REFUSED (`PER-ELEMENT-PROVENANCE`, decisions/registry.md) against its own three-condition bar, and `additionalProperties: false` makes reviving it under that name fail this gate loudly rather than pass unnoticed — the same discipline spec/figdown-model.schema.json states for its three deliberately-undeclared model slots. `semantic` is a designed, RESERVED slot with no producer: the shape lands (`MANIFEST-DEPENDENCY-AND-SEMANTIC-SLOTS`), the hash itself remains BLOCKED on the semantic-projection work, which is registered and not yet ruled, and a manifest shipped today simply omits the block — its absence is not `meaning unchanged` (figdown-manifest.md §7).

figdown_manifest.$comment: Versioned in its first key (figdown-manifest.md §3 rule 3, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`). A consumer that does not know the version stops; it does not guess — the same rule core §13.7 states for an engine reading a declared language version. There is only one profile version today, so `const` rather than `enum`: a second profile version is a version-gated event in this document, the same way a genre addition is a version-gated event in the language.

id.$comment: A publisher-scoped logical name, stable across renames of the file. NOT an element identity and NOT a cross-document identity — the identity model this project adopted deliberately left identity across documents closed, and this profile does not reopen it (figdown-manifest.md §4.1).

path.$comment: Repository-relative and ADVISORY, never restated-with-error-on-mismatch: a manifest that travels without its tree still has `id` (figdown-manifest.md §4.1). Not part of the restatement rule (§1) because no artifact field carries a repository path to disagree with.

sections.$comment: A COUNT, not a locator (figdown-manifest.md §2.2): a multi-section .fd has no syntax naming a section, and this key states how many there are, in document order, and nothing else about them.

version.$comment: The wire-grammar version the FIRST section's `figdown X.Y genre` header declares (figdown-manifest.md §4.2, following the §4.7/`ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE` convention that a multi-section file's single-valued restated field takes the first section's value and says so). A pattern, not an enum, for the same reason spec/figdown-model.schema.json's header.version is a pattern: the set gains one token per language release, which is bookkeeping, and the engine's own version gate is the authority, not this file.

genres.$comment: One entry per section, IN DOCUMENT ORDER and by nothing else (figdown-manifest.md §2.2, §4.2) — the array position is not a locator and MUST NOT be read as one.

renderer.title: Renderer identity, restated from the artifact (figdown-manifest.md §4.2, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`)

name.$comment: e.g. `figdown-svg` (package.json bin). Free string, no enum: renderer identity lives in the world, not in this profile (see the top-level $comment's ENUM POLICY).

engine_version.$comment: RESTATES the artifact's `data-engine-version` (core §7). A mismatch is an error IN THE MANIFEST, never a merge and never a vote (figdown-manifest.md §1, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`) — the `.fd`/`.svg` pair remains truth.

render_options.$comment: RESTATES the artifact's `data-render-options`, present in the manifest ONLY when the artifact carries a non-default option (core §7: 'Any non-default option MUST be recorded'). Its absence restates the artifact's default exactly as the artifact's own absent attribute does — the two are symmetric, and a manifest asserting a render option the artifact does not carry is a restatement mismatch (figdown-manifest.md §4.2, §1).

bytes.$comment: A cheap second signal over the same bytes the hash covers — catches a truncated copy before the hash is even computed (figdown-manifest.md §4.3).

semantic.title: semantic_sha256 — a designed, RESERVED slot (figdown-manifest.md §4.4, `MANIFEST-DEPENDENCY-AND-SEMANTIC-SLOTS`) — no producer exists yet
semantic.$comment: BLOCKED on the semantic-projection work, which is registered and not yet ruled (core §12.5.2, `MANIFEST-DEPENDENCY-AND-SEMANTIC-SLOTS`). Every manifest shipped today OMITS this block; absence is NOT 'meaning unchanged' — it means no producer exists yet (figdown-manifest.md §4.4, §7's absence sentence). When that work lands a hash, a consumer that does not recognise `algorithm`'s value MUST treat the field as UNREADABLE (report `unknown-semantic-algorithm` and fall back to `source.sha256`), never as 'unchanged' and never as 'changed' — silent fallback would let a meaning change pass as a byte change.

algorithm.$comment: Names (semantic projection version, canonicalization) as ONE token — a bare hash is unusable the day a second algorithm exists (figdown-manifest.md §4.4).

review.title: Review state — at most one, the strongest claim actually made (figdown-manifest.md §4.6, `MANIFEST-REVIEW-STATE`)

state.$comment: Four different claims, NOT a ladder (figdown-manifest.md §4.6, `MANIFEST-REVIEW-STATE`): `authored` claims nothing about an external source; `transcribed` claims the source was read, not checked; `reviewed` claims human judgement (`by` MUST name the party); `source-verified` claims correspondence against the cited source's own text. A figure may honestly carry `reviewed` or `source-verified` without the other.

of_source_sha256.$comment: The hash the state is ABOUT (figdown-manifest.md §4.6, `MANIFEST-REVIEW-STATE`). Differs from `source.sha256` => STALE, fatal — the figure changed after review, so the claim has no subject left. Absent => UNBOUND, reported, not fatal — a backfill note, not a failure. This is a RUNTIME assertion (verifier assertion C), not a schema constraint: JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling string values, so `tools/manifest-check.js` performs the STALE/UNBOUND check the schema only supplies the well-formed hash for.

provenance.title: Source provenance — an array of the publisher's own claims (figdown-manifest.md §4.5, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`)
provenance.$comment: One provenance object per source claim, because a transcribed figure routinely merges a drawing with the prose around it (figdown-manifest.md §4.5). Every entry MUST carry `relation` and at least one locator field (`section`, `figure`, `locator` or `bbox`) — verifier assertion D, checked by tools/manifest-check.js rather than by this schema, because the clean error message the design asks for ('no locator field present') is worth more than the generic 'matched none of N alternatives' a schema-level `anyOf` would produce.

accessibility.title: Accessibility state — a POINTER, and only a pointer (figdown-manifest.md §4.7, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`/`ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE`/`ACCESSIBLE-DESCRIPTION-SOURCES`)
accessibility.$comment: The STATES AND THEIR MEANINGS belong to the companion accessibility profile (decisions/registry.md, `ACCESSIBLE-DESCRIPTION-SOURCES`), not to this schema. This manifest decides only that the field exists, binds the same way `review` binds (`ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE`), and never restates the description text itself — the description lives in the artifact's `<desc>`; this records how far anyone has checked it. `role` (`MANIFEST-ACCESSIBILITY-ROLE`) is a second pointer of the same kind: its two-member vocabulary belongs to that profile's §2.1–§2.2, not to this schema — this field only supplies the declaration slot `ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE` requires a publisher choosing `role="img"` on the artifact to fill, closing the carried obligation recorded when the `accessibility` block first shipped with no place to declare it.

state.$comment: `ACCESSIBLE-DESCRIPTION-SOURCES`'s five states: `absent` (no description exists — not 'the figure needs none'); `derived` (a deterministic model projection, authoritative about the model and nothing else); `generated` (an LLM wrote it — never publishable on its own); `authored` (a human wrote it); `reviewed` (a human read it against the figure and accepted it, bound to the source hash the same way `review.of_source_sha256` binds).

role.$comment: CLOSED, exactly the two roles spec/figdown-a11y.md §2.1–§2.2 admits. OPTIONAL: absent means the profile's default requirement (`graphics-document`) and asserts nothing more — this field exists only to carry a DECLARATION, never a restatement of the artifact's own `role=` attribute (assertion B's restatement rule does not reach this field, because a publisher may legitimately declare the choice before or while producing the matching artifact). Flattening a graphic to `role="img"` is a decision about a reader, not a rendering detail (`ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE` §2.2), which is why the declaration exists at all (`MANIFEST-ACCESSIBILITY-ROLE`).

of_source_sha256.$comment: Bound the same way `review.of_source_sha256` binds (`ACCESSIBILITY-PROFILE`): a description reviewed against one source is not reviewed for the next. STALE/UNBOUND is a runtime check (verifier assertion C), not a schema constraint — see `review.of_source_sha256`'s $comment.

dependencies.title: Build-cache invalidation inputs — a cache signal, never a correctness claim (figdown-manifest.md §4.8, `MANIFEST-DEPENDENCY-AND-SEMANTIC-SLOTS`)
dependencies.$comment: A changed dependency says 'recompute', never 'the figure is wrong' — only the `.fd` <=> `.svg` pair can say the latter (host-profile.md §2.3). A stale dependency never authorizes a rebuild the artifact policy forbids (host-profile.md §2.3, §4) — this profile does not grant that authority and no field here can be read as granting it.

hash.$comment: Lower-case hex SHA-256, 64 characters — the same shape core §7's `data-sha256` uses. Every hash in this profile binds the FULL 64 hex, never truncated (figdown-manifest.md §4.6, `MANIFEST-REVIEW-STATE`: 'a machine-readable field has no reason to truncate').

date.$comment: ISO 8601 full-date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), checked by tools/manifest-check.js's minimal validator — the `LANE-ALPHABET-KEY-RESERVATION` guard discipline this repository's schema tooling follows: a `format` keyword nobody implements is a check nobody performs, so it is implemented here rather than left as an inert annotation.

relation.$comment: A small CLOSED vocabulary, three different claims (figdown-manifest.md §4.5, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`): `transcribed-from` (a re-drawing of that source figure), `derived-from` (built from that source's text, not from a picture), `about` (documents that thing but copies nothing). A reader who cannot tell them apart cannot use any of them.

document_sha256.$comment: The only field that turns a claim about a NAME into a claim about BYTES — and only for a consumer holding those bytes (figdown-manifest.md §4.5, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`).

locator.$comment: DELIBERATELY OPEN, unlike every other object in this schema: no ruling gives `locator`'s internal keys a closed vocabulary (decisions/registry.md shows only the example `{"paragraph": 342}`). A future ruling that closes this shape narrows it; until then a publisher may write whatever locator keys the source document's own structure calls for.

bbox.$comment: A bounding box with no coordinate system is four numbers, not a locator (figdown-manifest.md §4.5, `PUBLICATION-MANIFEST-PROFILE`): `page` and `unit` are both REQUIRED. The design text allows 'page (or another stated frame)' for a non-paginated source; no alternate frame key is ruled yet, so only `page` is implemented — a future ruling naming an alternate frame key extends this object, it does not replace `page`.

kind.$comment: The two kinds the ruled design's own examples use (decisions/registry.md): `source` (another FigDown `.fd` this figure's pipeline reads) and `external` (a non-FigDown input). Enumerated on the same policy as `relation`/`review.state`/`accessibility.state`: a third kind is a semantic event, not bookkeeping.
